import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.21

by L. G. Kovács

If the commutator subgroup $G'$ of a relatively free group $G$ is periodic, must $G'$
have finite exponent?

A group is *relatively free* if it is a free group of some variety of groups, i.e. it is
isomorphic to $F/V(F)$ for a free group $F$ and a verbal subgroup $V(F)$. Equivalently
(H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Springer, 1967), $G$ has a generating set $X$ such that
every map $X \to G$ extends to an endomorphism of $G$. The rank of $G$ is arbitrary
(possibly infinite).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.21»

/--
A group $G$ is *relatively free* if it has a generating set $X$ such that every map
$X \to G$ extends to an endomorphism of $G$. This is equivalent to $G$ being free in some
variety of groups (H. Neumann, *Varieties of Groups*, Springer, 1967): such a group is free
on $X$ in the variety generated by $G$, and conversely a free generating set of a group free in
some variety has the extension property.
-/
def IsRelativelyFree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Set G, Subgroup.closure X = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ f : X → G, ∃ φ : G →* G, ∀ x : X, φ x = f x

/-- A free group is relatively free (it is free in the variety of all groups). -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isRelativelyFree_freeGroup (α : Type*) : IsRelativelyFree (FreeGroup α) := by
  refine ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of α, fun f => ?_⟩
  refine ⟨FreeGroup.lift fun a => f ⟨FreeGroup.of a, a, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨_, a, rfl⟩
  simp

/-- The trivial group is relatively free (it is free in the trivial variety). -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isRelativelyFree_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    IsRelativelyFree G :=
  ⟨∅, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun _ => ⟨1, fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩⟩

/--
If the commutator subgroup $G'$ of a relatively free group $G$ is periodic, must $G'$
have finite exponent?

Here $G'$ is `commutator G`, "periodic" means every element of $G'$ has finite order
(`Monoid.IsTorsion`), and "finite exponent" means there is some $n \geq 1$ with $x^n = 1$
for all $x \in G'$ (`Monoid.ExponentExists`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.21» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRelativelyFree G →
      Monoid.IsTorsion (commutator G) → Monoid.ExponentExists (commutator G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.21»
